message_1_subject: Quickstart: infra & auth checklist + next steps
message_1_body:
Hi Elise / Tom,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the walkthrough of the Lumina search use case. Quick recap from our side and a suggested kickoff plan for the SDK quickstart + local testing:

Summary of needs (from call)
- Search/assistant surface with reranking: short latency SLOs for web search flows (~200ms p50 target)
- Strict data isolation in prod (private deployment / VPC), dev/prod parity for embeddings store
- SSO for developer team + SCIM for provisioning (preferred), fallback to API key for service accounts
- Required outputs: structured JSON output for tool-calling (order enrichment), embeddings for product catalog + reranker

Suggested immediate artifacts we can start with
1) Redwood quickstart playbook (attached) — runbook for local env + sample apps (Python + TS)
2) Mutual Action Plan template (attached) — timelines and owners
3) Small infra diagram for initial pilot (referenced below)

Asks / decisions we need from you this week
- Confirm auth preference: SSO (OIDC + SCIM) or API key flow? (we can support both, OIDC preferred for enterprise)
- Which sample app do you want first: "search + reranker" (embeddings index) or "chat + tool-calling" (structured output)?
- Do you need a private deployment preview (staging VPC) or will a hosted sandbox suffice for the pilot?

Proposed next step: technical kickoff — 45m with your infra + security and our engineering team. I propose Mon 2026-11-15 10:00 PT; I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Including Rafael and Sergio on the thread for technical notes and suggested quickstart commands.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes

message_3_subject: RE: Quickstart: infra & auth checklist + next steps — technical notes
message_3_body:
Camila / team — quick tech notes to prep the kickoff and the local quickstart. High level recommendations: 

Auth + provisioning
- Recommend OIDC (Okta) + SCIM for user provisioning; for CI/service accounts use short-lived API keys scoped to a single model/route.
- SCIM mapping: map groups -> redwood roles (dev/test/prod), enforce MFA for prod role.

Routing & model variants
- Create two routing policies for pilot: (1) low-latency route -> quantized L2 variant for freshness; (2) high-quality route -> full-precision L3 variant. Route based on query latency budget header (x-rdw-latency-budget).

Embeddings & reranker
- Start with a ~200k-vector index for pilot (64-dim / 1536-dim depending on model). Use sharded FAISS with exact recall for demo, switch to approximate for scale.
- Reranker can be async: initial top-K from ANN, then synchronous rerank using the full model for top-10. SDK supports both synchronous and streaming token outputs; for reranker we recommend syncing the final score back to UI via websocket.

Local quickstart commands (devs)
- python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
- pip install redwood-client==0.8.3
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<dev-api-key>"
- python examples/search_quickstart.py --local-index ./data/sample_vectors.npz

Notes: attach infra-diagram.png for expected VPC peering and private NAT for outbound controls. I'll prepare a one-pager with these items before the kickoff.

-Rafael
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
